text.text: Run the electrical business from one page. Estimates become Jobs, jobs get a lead electrician, and Mark done closes them after inspection. Materials shows what to restock, and Invoices shows what is still unpaid. Start with the Dashboard.

Overdue jobs
My jobs
Overdue invoices
A good estimate counts materials, labor, permit fees and the risk of what is behind the wall.
Steps
Visit the site and photograph the panel, meter and work area.
Count devices, wire runs and breakers.
Price materials, then labor hours at the shop rate.
Add permit and inspection fees as their own line.
Add overhead and a contingency for older buildings.
Presenting it
Send the estimate within a day. Offer good, better and best when there is a real choice, and state how long the price is valid.
Never energize new work before it is inspected where the law requires it.
Steps
Check whether the job needs a permit with the local office.
File with the address, scope and license number.
Book the rough-in inspection when the wiring is open, and the final when it is complete.
Mark the job On hold if an inspection fails and fix the notes the same day.
Records
Save the inspection sign-off in the job notes. It is the proof of work if the customer sells the home.
The same four steps before every job.
Checklist
Verify power is off with a tester at the panel and at the device.
Lock out and tag the breaker.
Wear the right gloves and eye protection for the task.
Tell the customer which circuits are off and for how long.
If something looks wrong
Stop, photograph it, and call the owner before touching it. Aluminum wiring, scorched panels and double-tapped breakers get a written recommendation.
